Class BasicWindow

java.lang.Object
io.github.isoyigido.basic.gui.window.BasicWindow
Direct Known Subclasses:
FullScreenWindow
public class BasicWindow extends Object
Stores basic properties for a window to be displayed. Provides setters for the properties. Provides the show(int, int) method to automatically set up and show the window with the stored properties.

  • Constructor Details

    • BasicWindow

      public BasicWindow(int windowWidth, int windowHeight)

      Constructs a basic window to be displayed.

      The virtual screen dimensions match the given window dimensions by default. Use setVirtualScreenDimensions(int, int) to set the virtual screen dimensions. The native aspect ratio of the physical screen displaying the window can be preserved on the virtual screen using preserveNativeAspectRatio().

      Use setTitle(String) to set the title of the window, and setIconImage(Image) to set the icon image of the window.

      The constructed window has the following default properties:

      • NOT resizable (use makeResizable() to make resizable)
      • NOT undecorated (use makeUndecorated() to make undecorated)
      • NOT always on top (use makeAlwaysOnTop() to make always on top)
      Parameters:
      windowWidth - the width of the window (in pixels)
      windowHeight - the height of the window (in pixels)

  • Method Details

    • setVirtualScreenDimensions

      public BasicWindow setVirtualScreenDimensions(int desiredScreenWidth, int desiredScreenHeight)
      Sets the virtual screen dimensions.
      Parameters:
      desiredScreenWidth - the desired width for the virtual screen (in pixels)
      desiredScreenHeight - the desired height for the virtual screen (in pixels)
      Returns:
      this
      API Note:
      The virtual screen dimensions set exactly match the desired dimensions, unless preserveNativeAspectRatio() is used. See preserveNativeAspectRatio() for more information.

    • preserveNativeAspectRatio

      public BasicWindow preserveNativeAspectRatio()
      Preserves the aspect ratio of the physical screen displaying the window on the virtual screen. When used, the virtual screen dimensions set may not match the desired dimensions, while the total pixel count is tried to be preserved.
      Returns:
      this
